newsitem.title: USA: VMI, Justice Department meet in court over women.
newsitem.headline: VMI, Justice Department meet in court over women.

text.p: Virginia Military Institute (VMI) maintained Wednesday it was working aggressively to integrate women into its cadet corps, despite accusations of stonewalling.

VMI, a state-funded military college, reluctantly opened its doors to women in September, three months after the U.S. Supreme Court ordered VMI to end 157 years of single-gender education or go private.

A VMI official told a federal court judge here that the school planned to admit women to the Lexington, Virginia-based campus next fall, but the Department of Justice wants VMI to reveal a detailed report on how it plans to integrate women within 30 days.
VMI responded it will not be pressured.
"We want to assert our independence in this process," VMI Superintendent Josiah Bunting told the court.
"This court has the obligation to show that what (VMI) is doing is effective," countered Judith Keith, lead attorney for the Justice department.
She added VMI "has a 150-year history of not admitting women, and more recently a six-year history of fighting not to admit women."
But Bunting told U.S. District Judge Jackson Kiser that VMI was aggressively recruiting women and had already hired the first female admissions officer since voting Sept. 21 to admit women.
Kiser did not indicate when he would rule.
